newsitem.title: MEXICO: SOCCER-MILUTINOVIC TO REMAIN MEXICO COACH, FOR NOW.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-MILUTINOVIC TO REMAIN MEXICO COACH, FOR NOW.

text.p: Mexican soccer officials announced after a meeting on Wednesday that national team coach Bora Milutinovic will keep his job -- but only until they meet again in less than one month's time.

A six-hour meeting of a Mexican Football Federation (FMF) committee voted that the Yugoslav coach, who led Mexico to the quarter-finals of the World Cup when the country hosted the tournament in 1986, should stay on.
But FMF official Eduardo Codesal then announced that another meeting would be held on December 18 because the federation's most important officials had not been present.
Mexico has reached the final six-team stage of the CONCACAF World Cup qualifying tournament but suffered humiliating defeats away to Jamaica and Honduras on the way.
This has led to huge criticism of Milutinovic, who also coached Costa Rica at the 1990 World Cup and the United States in 1994.
There was also anger when the Mexicans "only" scored five goals at home to Caribbean amateurs St. Vincent, who conceeded eleven goals in a later game against Honduras.
